articles.title: Ireland cut short news conference as mood darkens further before Israel game
articles.summary: Irish manager Hallgrimsson calls for ‘cool heads’ Accusations of racism dismissed as ‘completely untrue’ The Republic of Ireland’s press conference on the eve of their second Nations League match against Israel in Serbia was cut short as the head coach, Heimir Hallgrimsson, fielded questions from…
body: Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Hungary in their first match on Tuesday following a turbulent buildup in which the Irish squad voted to fulfil the fixture despite unease among the team over the war in Gaza.
During that match the Irish players wore armbands and pointedly lowered their heads while the Israeli national anthem played. There were no handshakes between the captains before kick-off.

With the return leg taking place on Sunday in Backa Topola after the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) refused to host the match at home for security reasons, it was the Ireland manager’s pre-match press conference on Saturday that gave rise to new tensions.
One reporter questioned Hallgrimsson on his thoughts about the incident on Wednesday during a Flydubai flight from the UAE to Israel.

articles.title: 'Different' Morrison gives NI new option
articles.summary: Northern Ireland's Kieran Morrison hopes he has earned the trust of manager Michael O'Neill after impressing on his first international start.
body: The Liverpool winger, who is spending this season on loan at Sheffield Wednesday, provided the assist for Isaac Price for the side's second goal in an eye-catching 3-0 Nations League win over Ukraine in Slovakia.
The 19-year-old was one of three changes made by O'Neill for the game in Trnava and impressed in an inside forward role off the right-hand side.
An unused substitute for the first two games of Group B2 in which Northern Ireland took four points against Georgia and Hungary, Morrison was pleased to quickly repay O'Neill's faith.
"I've been biding my time after the first two games," he told BBC Sport NI's Gavin Andrews.

articles.title: Zigiotti Olme capitalises on Liverpool mistake to keep Manchester United moving up WSL
articles.summary: Julia Zigiotti Olme’s sixth-minute lob proved enough to earn the Manchester United coach, Eva Olid, a second Women’s Super League victory of the season with a 1-0 home win over Liverpool.
body: Zigiotti Olme capitalised on a mistake by Liverpool goalkeeper, Khiara Keating, and, despite some late pressure by Gareth Taylor’s side, United held on to make it back-to-back league wins.
After a shaky start under the new head coach, Olid, the Spaniard has now masterminded four consecutive victories in all competitions with United unbeaten in five matches.
This was United’s 250th match since the team reformed in 2018 and Olid watched her side mark the occasion with the breakthrough after six minutes.
It was a moment to forget for England goalkeeper Keating after her pass out from the back was intercepted by Zigiotti Olme, who composed herself and chipped home in superb fashion.

articles.title: Michigan state police rule out claim that Larry Nassar was removed from sex offender registry
articles.summary: Eaton county prosecuting attorney’s office had said court ruling forced removal of Nassar’s name – but he wasn’t on list because he was imprisoned out of state. Michigan has removed more than 20,000 entries from its sex offender registry, but convicted serial abuser Larry Nassar is not one of them…
body: On 9 September, the Michigan supreme court ruled that the state’s Sex Offender Registration Act (Sora) cannot be applied retroactively to cases involving offenses committed before the law’s relevant date. Michigan’s state police, as a result, removed more than 20,000 people whose offenses occurred before 1 July 2011 from the agency’s online sex offender database.

One of the agencies to prosecute Nassar, the Eaton county prosecuting attorney’s office, asserted that he was among those removed from the Michigan state police sex offender registry. The office – helmed by Republican Michigan state attorney general candidate Doug Lloyd – even shared a screenshot showing a search for his name returning zero results.
The office also published a statement that read: “The Michigan supreme court’s decision to eliminate Sora requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning.”

The statement was widely reported on in the news media, and it added: “Our community, along with the victims of these crimes, expected the registry to provide a measure of protection and awareness – assurances that have now been removed by the court’s ruling.”

articles.summary: MADISON – The status of one of Wisconsin football ’s top offensive weapons is up in the air in the hours leading up to the Badgers ’ Week 5 game against Michigan State. First-team running back Abu Sama III was officially listed as a game-time decision on the Big Ten’s pregame availability report.
body: Sama exited the Penn State game with an upper-body injury and then was listed as questionable on the Wednesday, Thursday and Friday availability reports.

If Sama cannot play, Darrion Dupree would be the Badgers ’ most likely starter at running back. Dupree had 52 rushing yards and 44 receiving yards in UW’s 24-20 win over then-No. 14 Penn State in Week 4.
Sama was the only game-time decision for the Badgers. Cornerback Cai Bates, wide receiver Jaylon Domingeaux, running back Mason Lane and offensive lineman Michael Roeske are listed as out.

articles.title: Solberg piles pressure on Evans in WRC title race
articles.summary: Elfyn Evans' hopes of claiming a first World Rally Championship title are in the balance after another strong morning for rival Oliver Solberg in Sardinia.
body: Elfyn Evans' hopes of claiming a first World Rally Championship (WRC) crown are hanging by a thread after rival Oliver Solberg took the lead in the title-deciding Rally Italia Sardegna.
Solberg was again the fastest driver across Saturday morning's three stages, leapfrogging the overnight top two, Hyundai pair Thierry Neuville and Adrien Fourmaux.
The 25-year-old Swede leads Neuville by 2.7 seconds, while Evans lies in sixth place, one minute 57.7 seconds behind the new rally leader.
The Welshman had taken a 17-point lead into the final round of the season, but on current positions that gap would be reduced to four.

articles.title: Keenan Allen injury update leaves Colts thin at WR before London game
articles.summary: Keenan Allen ‘s still contributing in a big way in his 14th NFL season, but he won’t be available this weekend. Week 4 has teams scrambling after several key injuries have disrupted the flow of play.
body: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Allen is out for Indy’s London matchup against their NFC East opponent. The 34-year-old has been battling a groin injury, and that leaves the Colts thin at wideout on Sunday.
That means quarterback Daniel Jones will have to rely on other weapons in the passing game, as well as a heavy dose of Jonathan Taylor in the rushing attack.

The Colts have been pleasantly surprised by Allen’s contributions in 2026 after joining the franchise. Indianapolis head coach Shane Steichen brought in the veteran wideout to complement some of the team’s younger assets.
The franchise is already without Alec Pierce after the Colts placed him on IR last month with a heel injury. It’s the same setback that already lingered with the receiver coming into this season.

articles.title: Qatar and Abu Dhabi F1 Grand Prix to go ahead - F1 boss
articles.summary: The final races of the Formula One season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will go ahead as planned despite tensions in the Middle East, the sport's CEO Stefano Domenicali said Saturday.
body: "Based on the information we have, everything is confirmed for (us to stay in) Qatar and Abu Dhabi," Domenicali told French broadcaster Canal Plus on the sidelines of the Bahrain Grand Prix, which was relocated to the Sepang circuit in Malaysia this weekend.
Speaking to Sky Sport Italia, the boss of motorsport's premier series "confirmed the schedule for the final two Grands Prix" of the year in Qatar on November 29 and Abu Dhabi on December 6.
The Bahrain and Saudi Arabia grands prix were scrapped earlier this season due to the start of the US-led war with Iran.
Italian Domenicali insisted "that everything was in order" and that "teams and drivers were being kept informed of the situation."

articles.title: Hamilton hopes for 'awesome' Verstappen fight for win
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton says it will be important for Ferrari to focus on their own race for what is expected to be a challenging Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia but admits it would be "awesome" if they have the pace to stay with polesitter Max Verstappen from the front row.
body: ​Hamilton produced "probably my best lap of the year" to claim second on the grid with his last attempt of qualifying at the Sepang International Circuit, his second front-row start of the year.

It will be the first time Verstappen and Hamilton, the grid's two-most successful drivers and the sport's biggest names, have started at the head of a Grand Prix together since July 2023, at that year's Hungarian Grand Prix.
Championship leader Kimi Antonelli is just behind them in third, creating a mouth-watering head of the grid for lights out at 8am on Sunday live on Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event.
Verstappen claimed pole, Red Bull's first of the season, by 0.298s and the Dutchman's form so far this weekend on F1's return to Sepang suggests he is the favourite to win too.

articles.title: Fairy Glen foils Sunly in Prix de Royallieu
articles.summary: Fairy Glen came from last to first in the Qatar Prix de Royallieu to floor odds-on favourite Sunly and land a Group One prize for Newmarket training duo Simon and Ed Crisford.
body: Simon and Ed Crisford's Fairy Glen chased down Sunly to win the 2026 Prix de Royallieu on day one of Arc weekend at ParisLongchamp; Also on the day, the George Scott-trained Wimbledon Hawkeye struck gold in the Prix Dollar.
Sunly, who was backed into favouritism at 5-6, had taken up the running a furlong from home, but with a target to aim at Barzalona and Fairy Glen came late and wide to grab top spot by a neck.
St Leger third Amelia Earhart battled on well to hold third place, another three-quarters of a length back.

Fairy Glen, who is set to be retired at the end of the season, won the Group Two Balanchine and Dubai Gold Cup in Meydan in the spring and finished fifth in the Prix Vicomtesse Vigier behind Caballo De Mar here in May.
